summary: Enum naming the 13 easing curves EasingFunctions.Evaluate can apply, from Linear to OutBounce.
problem: Easing is a choice a designer makes, not a formula a programmer hard-codes, so the curve needs to be a value you can put on a serialized field and pick from an Inspector dropdown. This enum is that value. It covers the four families that cover almost every real requirement — Quad and Cubic for plain acceleration, Back for anticipation and overshoot, Elastic and Bounce for springy arrivals — each in the In (slow start), Out (slow finish) and InOut (slow at both ends) flavours where they make sense. Note the set is deliberately incomplete: there is no InBounce, InOutBounce or InOutElastic, so do not assume symmetry when porting values from another tweening library.
useCases: A [SerializeField] EaseType on a UI animation component, so the curve is picked in the Inspector rather than recompiled.
Storing the curve choice in a ScriptableObject preset shared by every toast, modal and tooltip in the project.
Passing an ease choice through a tween API: Tween.To(..., EaseType.OutCubic).
Driving a shader parameter or camera move with the same named curve the UI uses, so motion feels consistent across systems.
